title: Unauthenticated Next.js Server Action DoS in next@16.2.4
description: The project deploys next@16.2.4, which is inside the affected range for GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj (>=16.0.0 <16.2.11). The application uses the App Router and binds an unauthenticated admin-login Server Action to a public form. A crafted request can consume excessive CPU and block further requests in the same process.
root_cause: The Next.js dependency in package.json pins an affected framework version for the public App Router runtime.
intended_behavior: The public App Router and Server Actions should run on a supported framework version containing all published security fixes.

trace.description: An unauthenticated public Server Action accepts attacker-controlled FormData through the Next.js App Router.
The request is handled by the declared next@16.2.4 runtime, which is inside the advisory's affected range.

conditions.description: The application uses the Next.js App Router with at least one reachable Server Action.
The attacker can reach the public application and the request is not rejected by an upstream proxy before reaching Next.js.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated remote client able to reach the public Next.js application.
payloads: The crafted Server Action request described by GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj; exact bytes were not published or dynamically reproduced in this source audit.
instructions: Send the advisory trigger to the public admin-login Server Action endpoint.
Observe excessive CPU and blocked requests in the same Next.js process.
execution.expected_result: The vulnerable Next.js worker consumes resources and degrades or loses availability.

remediation.strategy: Upgrade to 16.3.4 or a newer current patched release, refresh the lockfile and rebuild. Version 16.2.11 is the minimum fix for this advisory alone.

likelihood.reason: The App Router is internet-facing and authentication is not required to reach framework parsing.

impact.reason: Successful exploitation can make the public service unavailable.

confidence.reason: The installed affected version and public reachability are verified; the advisory trigger was not executed against a production build during this source audit.

title: Known vulnerable Sharp/libvips version parses author-controlled images
description: The project installs sharp@0.34.5, which the current npm advisory database reports as affected by libvips/libheif memory-safety advisories. A normal authenticated author can upload avatar and cover bytes which are decoded by Sharp. File size, pixel and page limits reduce resource abuse but do not patch native codec defects.
root_cause: The Sharp dependency in package.json remains on an affected native image-processing release, allowing crafted author-controlled image bytes to reach vulnerable codecs.
intended_behavior: Authenticated image uploads should be decoded only by a patched image-processing library and safely re-encoded before storage or display.

trace.description: An ordinary authenticated author supplies avatarFile as multipart FormData.
The full attacker-supplied file is copied into a Buffer.
The Buffer is passed to the affected Sharp native decoder.

conditions.description: The attacker needs an ordinary author account and valid session.

payloads: A crafted JPEG/PNG/WebP/HEIF-family image exercising an affected libvips/libheif codec path while remaining within upload limits.
instructions: Submit the crafted file as avatarFile with valid crop fields, or through a cover upload.
Observe the native image worker/process failure.
execution.expected_result: Native decoder memory corruption or process crash, causing at least denial of service.

remediation.strategy: Upgrade Sharp to the fixed version reported by npm audit, perform a clean native rebuild, and regression-test every upload pipeline.

likelihood.reason: Requires an author account and a codec-specific crafted file, but the upload-to-decoder path is direct.

impact.reason: Native memory-safety defects can crash the process and may have stronger consequences depending on the codec defect.

confidence.reason: Affected version and reachable native sink are verified; no exploit image was executed in this audit.

title: Unbounded bug-report creation amplifies notifications and transport deliveries
description: Any authenticated author can repeatedly create identical bug reports. Every accepted request transactionally persists a report and domain event. When the dispatcher processes it, the consumer creates one inbox notification per current administrator and, if the transport route is enabled, a transport-outbox row per configured chat or a missing-recipient sentinel. There is no endpoint rate limit, quota, cooldown or duplicate constraint.
root_cause: POST in src/app/api/bug-reports/route.ts does not rate-limit or deduplicate authenticated submissions, allowing persistent notification and queue amplification.
intended_behavior: Authors should be able to report legitimate bugs without being able to flood administrator inboxes, external transports or persistence queues.

trace.description: An authenticated author submits JSON containing a bounded description and same-origin URL.
Each request inserts a new bug report and unique bug-report.created domain event.
After domain-event dispatch, the handler inserts admin inbox notifications and then optional configured transport-outbox rows.

conditions.description: The attacker needs an ordinary author account and valid session.
Inbox fan-out requires at least one current administrator and successful domain-event dispatch; report/event growth occurs regardless.
Telegram spam additionally requires the bug_report_created transport route to be enabled; an enabled route with no chat IDs still creates a missing-recipient outbox row.

execution.attacker_perspective: Ordinary authenticated author using their own session.
payloads: POST /api/bug-reports with Cookie: author_session_v2=<valid>, Content-Type: application/json, body {"description":"x","url":"/"}
instructions: Send the valid request repeatedly or concurrently.
Observe a fresh 201 and report ID for every request.
After successful domain-event dispatch, observe admin notifications and optional transport deliveries.
execution.expected_result: Guaranteed unbounded report/event growth; after dispatch, admin-notification growth when admins exist and transport-outbox growth when its route is enabled.

remediation.strategy: Apply fail-closed per-author and per-IP rate limits before the transaction, return 429, and add a short duplicate cooldown or pending-report quota.

code_changes.fixed_code: Check a bug-report-specific per-author and trusted-client-IP limiter before createBugReport; return HTTP 429 when exceeded.

likelihood.reason: The attack is trivial for any account and uses a normal valid request.

impact.reason: Damage is operational spam and storage/queue growth requiring sustained traffic, not confidentiality or privilege loss.

confidence.reason: Two independent code reviews traced the full route-to-database-to-fan-out path and found no rate limit, quota or deduplication layer.
